about: Plain words for SPARC's technical terms, shared by SPARC Studio (studio-web/src/content/glossary.ts) and the standalone results page. Each term: a plain label for the page, a 1-2 sentence tip (max 240 characters), the technical name, and optionally a longer explanation. The lever, mode, confidence, trust and engine sections hold the Scenario Lab's wording verbatim.

r2.label: Accuracy score
r2.tip: How much of the temperature differences between places the model gets right in areas it was not trained on. 1 is perfect; 0 is no better than guessing the city average.
r2.more: R² is measured on areas held out from training, so it shows how well the model predicts places it has never seen. At or above 0.6 counts as Good, 0.4 to 0.6 as Fair, and below 0.4 as Limited.

rmse.label: Typical error
rmse.tip: How far a prediction typically lands from the measured temperature, in areas the model was not trained on. In the run's temperature units; smaller is better.

coverage.label: Range reliability
coverage.tip: How often the real measurement falls inside the model's prediction range. A 90% range should hold about 9 times in 10; much less means the ranges are too narrow.
coverage.more: Coverage is checked on areas held out from training. Within 5 percentage points of its target, the ranges count as holding; further off, the trust grade drops one step.

interval_honesty.label: Do the ranges hold?
interval_honesty.tip: Checks, test area by test area, whether the prediction ranges contain the real measurements as often as they claim to.

trust_grade.label: Trust grade
trust_grade.tip: Good, Fair or Limited: how well the model predicts places it was not trained on, and whether its prediction ranges hold.
trust_grade.technical: Held-out R² with an interval-coverage check

stacker.label: Model blend
stacker.tip: The final prediction blends several models. Each one counts according to how well it predicts areas it was not trained on.

blend_weights.label: Blend weights
blend_weights.tip: How much each model counts in the final blend. A bigger weight means that model did better in areas it was not trained on.

physics_card.label: Physics model settings
physics_card.tip: The values the built-in heat-physics model settled on, such as how far heat spreads, and how much they vary between test areas.

advection.label: Wind carrying heat
advection.tip: Whether the model lets the wind carry warm air from one place to its neighbours, and whether that made its predictions better.

forcing.label: Weather inputs
forcing.tip: The weather that drives the model for the day it describes: sunshine, heat from the sky and wind, from a weather station or a weather dataset.

cv_design.label: How the model was tested
cv_design.tip: The city is split into areas. The model is trained without one area and tested on it, so every score comes from places it had not seen.

held_out_fold.label: Test area
held_out_fold.tip: One of the areas kept out of training and used only to test the model.

ring_kernel.label: Reach of a change
ring_kernel.tip: How a change in one place also cools the places around it, fading with distance in rings.

footprint.label: Total cooling, nearby included
footprint.tip: All the cooling a change in one place causes: on the spot, plus in the places around it.

anisotropy.label: Direction matters
anisotropy.tip: Whether a feature's influence reaches further in one direction than another, e.g. downwind. 1 means the same in every direction.

priors.label: Starting assumptions
priors.tip: The values the model starts from before it sees the data, such as how far heat typically spreads. The data then adjusts them.

length_scale.label: Influence distance
length_scale.tip: How far, in metres, a feature such as tree cover still affects the temperature around it.

cate.label: Effect by place
cate.tip: How much the same change cools in different kinds of places. Some places gain more than others.

dag_audit.label: Cause-and-effect check
dag_audit.tip: Checks the model's cooling against a separate cause-and-effect analysis, to rule out effects that are only coincidence.

partial_dependence.label: Response curve
partial_dependence.tip: How the predicted temperature changes as one feature goes up or down, with everything else left as it is.

dose_response.label: Cooling by amount
dose_response.tip: How much cooling each amount of change brings, from a small step to a large one.

saturation.label: Diminishing returns
saturation.tip: Whether each extra step of a change cools less than the last, and by how much change most of the possible cooling is reached.
saturation.more: Each place's cooling curve is sorted into one of four shapes: Diminishing, Steady, Slow start then strong, or Hit the limit (still cooling at the largest amount the space allows).

d90.label: Amount for 90% of the cooling
d90.tip: The amount of change by which a typical place gets 90% of all the cooling it can get. Past it, extra effort buys little.

own_cell.label: Effect on the spot
own_cell.tip: The cooling in the place you change only, leaving out what spills over to its neighbours.

dose_scale.label: Size of the change
dose_scale.tip: How big the tested amounts are next to how much the layer already varies across the city. Very large ones go beyond what was measured.

open_loop.label: Planned benefit
open_loop.tip: The cooling a plan should bring, adding up each place's expected response. A quick sum, not yet checked with the full model.

closed_loop.label: Checked benefit
closed_loop.tip: The whole plan run through the full model, so neighbours, limits and knock-on effects all count.
closed_loop.technical: Closed loop (plan re-run through the exact engine)

mediators.label: Knock-on effects
mediators.tip: Related measures that move with a change, e.g. greenness follows tree cover. Including them gives a fuller picture.

gini.label: Unevenness of benefit
gini.tip: How unevenly the cooling is shared. 0 means every place gains the same; near 1 means a few places get almost all of it.

kendall_tau.label: Ranking agreement
kendall_tau.tip: How closely two rankings of places agree. 1 is the same order, 0 is no relation, −1 is the reverse order.

multiverse.label: Stability across choices
multiverse.tip: Whether the answer holds when the analysis is redone with other reasonable choices, such as different settings or data versions.

noise_floor.label: Smallest possible error
noise_floor.tip: The error that comes only from the measurements being rounded. No model can do better than this.

compile.label: Check the change
compile.tip: Works out which places a change touches and how much of it fits the space available, before anything runs.

portable.label: Reusable in other runs
portable.tip: The places are drawn on the map rather than taken from this run's grid, so other runs can use the same scenario.

run_exact.label: Run full model
run_exact.tip: Runs your changes through the full model for the firm answer, with a likely range. Takes a few minutes.

exact_engine.label: Full model
exact_engine.tip: The complete model trained for this run. Slower than the quick estimate, but it gives the firm answer with a likely range.

emulator_preview.label: Quick estimate
emulator_preview.tip: An instant, approximate answer that updates as you make changes. Run the full model for the firm answer.

uniform_rel_error.label: Quick-estimate error, citywide
uniform_rel_error.tip: How far off the quick estimate can be when a change covers the whole city, as a share of the full model's answer.

hatched.label: Less certain here
hatched.tip: Hatching marks places where a number is less reliable: rough on a quick estimate, or beyond anything measured on a full-model result.

extrapolated.label: Beyond measured conditions
extrapolated.tip: The change pushes some places past anything measured in the city today, so the model is less sure there.

jackknife_se.label: Spread between test areas
jackknife_se.tip: How much the answer moves when each test area's model is left out in turn. It sets how wide the likely range is.

interval_95.label: Likely range
interval_95.tip: The real effect very probably lies in this range (95% of the time). A range that crosses zero means there might be no real effect.

estimation.label: Model fit (the likely range)
estimation.tip: Doubt from the model itself: how much the answer varies between models trained on different areas.

specification.label: Across model versions and runs
specification.tip: Doubt from how the analysis was set up: how much the answer moves across other runs and model versions.

attribution.label: Simulation check
attribution.tip: Made-up data with a known effect, run through the same analysis, shows how far off the cooling estimate can be.

causal_band.label: Independent cause-and-effect check
causal_band.tip: The range from a separate cause-and-effect analysis that does not use the main model.

envelope.label: All sources together
envelope.tip: The widest range, once every source of doubt is added up. If it stays on one side of zero, the direction of the effect is solid.

clipped.label: Did not fit
clipped.tip: The part of what you asked for that the space does not allow, e.g. more trees than there is ground to plant. It is left out.

realised.label: What actually changed
realised.tip: The change that went in once limits were applied. It can be less than you asked for.

realistic_limits.label: Keep changes within realistic limits
realistic_limits.tip: Never push a place beyond the range seen anywhere in the city today (the model is only trustworthy inside it).

expert_mode.label: Expert mode
expert_mode.tip: Edit any model input, not only the planning levers.

headroom.label: Available planting space
headroom.tip: Open ground in a place that could take trees, leaving out buildings and roads.

cell.label: Place
cell.tip: The map is split into equal squares, and each square is one place. Results are worked out for every place.

citywide.label: Citywide
citywide.tip: Averaged over the whole city, including the places you did not change.

where_changed.label: Where you made changes
where_changed.tip: Averaged over the places you changed only.

delta_t.label: Temperature change
delta_t.tip: How much warmer or cooler a place gets. A negative number means cooler.

cost_per_degree.label: Cost per degree
cost_per_degree.tip: What it costs to cool one place by 1 degree, with the cooling added up over every place.

reach.label: How far cooling reaches
reach.tip: How much of the cooling lands outside the places you changed, in rings by distance.

pareto.label: Best trade-offs
pareto.tip: Each point is the most cooling a given budget can buy. A plan below the line gets less for the same money.

placebo.label: Fake-change test
placebo.tip: Runs the analysis on changes that should do nothing. Finding no effect shows the pipeline does not invent one.

independent_checks.label: Independent checks
independent_checks.tip: Extra tests run on top of the model: a fake-change test, a simulation with a known effect, other reasonable analysis choices and a full repeat of the run. They show whether the results hold up.

keep_in_mind.label: Things to keep in mind
keep_in_mind.tip: Points about this run, worked out from its own numbers, to read before using its results.

distance_skill.label: Accuracy away from measurements
distance_skill.tip: The model is tested again with bigger areas held out, so each test place lies farther from any reading. If the accuracy score holds up, the map can be trusted between measurements.
distance_skill.technical: Skill vs CV block size (held-out R² or RMSE)

causal_audit.label: Cause or coincidence
causal_audit.tip: A separate statistical analysis of the readings, which does not use the model, estimates each lever's effect. When the two agree, the model's effect is unlikely to be a coincidence.

verdict_robust.label: Solid
verdict_robust.tip: Even with every source of doubt counted, the likely range stays on one side of zero, and every version of the analysis agrees on whether the change cools or warms.

verdict_direction.label: Direction clear
verdict_direction.tip: We can say whether the change cools or warms, but not by how much: the effect could be close to zero.

verdict_not_established.label: Not proven
verdict_not_established.tip: The effect cannot be told apart from no effect: it is no bigger than fake changes produce, the checks disagree, or most changed places lie beyond measured conditions.

e_value.label: Sensitivity to hidden causes
e_value.tip: How strongly an unmeasured factor would have to be tied to both the change and the temperature to explain the effect away. Bigger is sturdier; 1 means it would take nothing.

bias_correction.label: Correction for under-estimation
bias_correction.tip: If the simulation check finds the model recovers the same share of a planted effect (say 80%) for every kind of made-up data, citywide effects can be scaled by it. If the share varies, read them as a range.
bias_correction.technical: Bias correction (median effect share across generators)

effect_share.label: Share of a known effect recovered
effect_share.tip: A known effect is planted in made-up data and the analysis is run on it. 1 means it was recovered exactly; below 1 the model understates it, above 1 it overstates it.

false_positive.label: False alarms
false_positive.tip: How often the analysis finds an effect in made-up data where none was planted. About 5% is expected by chance.

baselines.label: Simpler models
baselines.tip: Simple reference models, such as the city average or a nearest-neighbour guess, scored on the same test areas. The full model should beat them.
baselines.technical: Reference baselines (ΔMSE on the same CV blocks)

reproduce.label: Repeat run
reproduce.tip: Runs the analysis again from the same inputs and settings, and checks that the numbers come out the same.

literature_check.label: Published studies
literature_check.tip: Cooling found by published studies of similar changes, next to this run's estimate. Agreement is a sanity check only: other cities and methods differ.

benchmark.label: Known-effect test
benchmark.tip: Plants a known tree-cover effect in a made-up city and measures how much of it each model recovers. It needs no run.

residual.label: Prediction miss
residual.tip: The measured minus the predicted temperature at a place. Positive means the model predicted too cool there; negative, too warm.

heat_index.label: Feels-like temperature
heat_index.tip: Air temperature and humidity combined into how hot it feels to the body, in °F.

heat_risk_level.label: Heat-risk level
heat_risk_level.tip: The US National Weather Service bands of the feels-like temperature: Caution, Extreme caution, Danger and Extreme danger.

ssp.label: Emissions future
ssp.tip: A storyline of how much greenhouse gas the world emits this century, from low to very high. Higher emissions bring more warming.

climate_period.label: Time period
climate_period.tip: The 20 years a future climate is averaged over, e.g. mid-century (2041–2060).

warming_offset.label: Share of warming cancelled
warming_offset.tip: How much of the coming warming the change cancels out where you made it.

humidity_assumption.label: Humidity assumption
humidity_assumption.tip: How muggy the afternoon is taken to be, as a dew point in °F. Humid air makes heat feel worse, so this changes the feels-like temperature. One value is used for the whole city.
humidity_assumption.technical: Dewpoint (°C) for the NWS heat index

future_humidity.label: Future humidity
future_humidity.tip: Nobody knows how muggy warmer afternoons will be, so two cases bracket it: the air holds the same amount of water as today, so it feels a little less muggy (low end), or it takes up more water and stays as muggy as today (high end).
future_humidity.technical: Constant dewpoint (lower bound) / constant relative humidity (upper bound)

climate_models.label: Climate models
climate_models.tip: Each climate model gives its own answer for how much warmer it gets. We show the middle answer; most models fall within the range shown.
climate_models.technical: CMIP6 ensemble: median, 10th–90th percentile across models

campaign.label: Measured afternoon
campaign.tip: The hot afternoon when the temperature readings this run is built on were taken.

person_mean.label: Average temperature where people live
person_mean.tip: The average temperature residents experience: each place counts by how many people live there, so busy neighbourhoods weigh more than empty land.

hot_days.label: Hot days per year
hot_days.tip: How many summer afternoons a year reach each temperature: the local weather station's daily record, shifted by how much hotter or cooler each place measured.
hot_days.technical: GHCN-Daily station record (1995–2014) plus each cell's campaign offset

quintile.label: Fifth
quintile.tip: Places are ranked by a measure, such as population density, and split into five equal groups, from the lowest fifth to the highest.

concentration_index.label: Who gets the cooling
concentration_index.tip: Whether the cooling leans toward places ranked high or low on this measure. 0 means it is shared evenly; above 0, more goes to the higher fifths; below 0, to the lower fifths.

climate_offset.label: Warming cancelled
climate_offset.tip: How much of the expected warming a scenario cancels out, averaged over the whole city: its citywide cooling as a share of the climate models' middle estimate of warming.
climate_offset.technical: Offset share of median warming (citywide mean ΔT ÷ median CMIP6 warming)

demo.label: Demo data
demo.tip: Made-up data for a fictional place, for trying SPARC out. Its numbers say nothing about a real city.

checkpoint.label: Saved models
checkpoint.tip: The trained models, saved during the run. The full model, the quick estimate and resuming an interrupted run all need them; without them the models must be trained again.

predictor.label: Map layer
predictor.tip: A map layer the model uses to predict temperature, such as tree cover, paving or building height. The levers are the layers a plan can change.

coarse.label: Coarser grid
coarse.tip: For a faster run, the input squares were averaged into bigger ones. The broad patterns hold, but street-level detail is lost.

grid_fill.label: Share of the grid with readings
grid_fill.tip: The share of squares in the grid's rectangle that hold at least one reading. The rest lie outside the study area or have no data.

fractional_part.label: Rounding in the readings
fractional_part.tip: The digits after the decimal point of every reading. Real measurements spread evenly; readings piled on whole numbers or .5 were rounded or classed, which caps how precise any model can be.

uncommitted_code.label: Unsaved code changes
uncommitted_code.tip: The code had changes not yet committed to version control when the run started, so its commit alone cannot repeat the run exactly.

provenance.label: Audit trail
provenance.tip: Where the run came from: fingerprints of its input files and settings, and the exact code and software, so anyone can check or repeat it.

dose.label: Amount of change
dose.tip: How much a lever changes in a place, in the lever's own units, e.g. +10 percentage points of tree cover.

ladder.label: Amount ladder
ladder.tip: The same change run at several growing amounts, to see how the cooling grows with the amount and where it levels off.

sweep.label: Try amounts
sweep.tip: Runs one lever at several amounts through the full model, each with its likely range, to see how the cooling grows and where it levels off.

neighbourhood_dose.label: Amount nearby
neighbourhood_dose.tip: The change averaged over the area around each place, weighted by distance. For a change in one area it is smaller than the amount asked for there.

paired_se.label: Uncertainty of the difference
paired_se.tip: How precisely the gap between two results is known. They are compared test area by test area, so doubt they share cancels out. It needs the full model's result for each test area.
paired_se.technical: Paired standard error, SE(A − B) over held-out folds

total_cooling.label: Total cooling
total_cooling.tip: Cooling added up over every place it reaches, in degree·places (°F·places): 1 place cooled by 1 degree and 10 places cooled by 0.1 degree both count as 1.
total_cooling.technical: ΔT summed over cells (target units · cells)

cost_units.label: Cost units
cost_units.tip: Spending in the units the project's costs are set in. By default one unit of change in one place costs 1, so +10 pts in 100 places costs 1,000.
cost_units.technical: Budget units (cost per unit × amount, summed over cells)

stale.label: Out of date
stale.tip: The model has changed since this result was worked out. It stays viewable; run the full model again to refresh it.

configured_scenario.label: Set up with this run
configured_scenario.tip: Scenarios written in the project's settings and worked out when the run finished. They are read-only here: clone one to change it.

budget_plan.label: Budget plan
budget_plan.tip: Spends a fixed budget where the change cools most for its cost, one step at a time, until the budget runs out.

readiness.label: Readiness
readiness.tip: How many of the project's setup checks pass: the data and its columns, what you can change, and the weather, climate and people data. A run can start once the data is in.

levers.label: What you can change
levers.tip: The map layers a plan can change, such as tree cover, paving or roof colour. SPARC works out how much cooling each change brings.

peak_ram.label: Memory needed
peak_ram.tip: The most computer memory (RAM) the run is expected to use at one time. If the computer has less free, the run slows down or stops.

threads.label: Processor threads
threads.tip: How many parts of the computer's processor a job may use at once. More makes it faster but leaves less for other work.

config_version.label: Settings version
config_version.tip: Each save of the project's settings makes a new numbered version. A run records the version it used, so you can see what changed between runs.

code_version.label: Code version
code_version.tip: The version of the SPARC software that made the run. Runs made with the same code can be compared like for like.

run_fast.label: Fast
run_fast.tip: A first look in minutes: fewer models and less tuning. Good for checking the setup, not for final decisions.

run_coarse.label: Coarse
run_coarse.tip: The whole analysis on bigger squares: a faithful preview in a fraction of the time, without street-level detail.

run_full.label: Full
run_full.tip: Every model at full detail. It takes the longest; use it for the results that decisions rest on.

stage_s0.label: Check the data
stage_s0.tip: Reads the temperature readings, flags doubtful ones and places them on the map grid.

stage_s1.label: Measure reach
stage_s1.tip: Measures how far each map layer, such as tree cover, still affects the temperature around it, and sizes the test areas to match.

stage_s2_s3.label: Train the models
stage_s2_s3.tip: Trains several models, each tested on areas it did not see, and blends them into one prediction.

stage_baselines.label: Simple-model check
stage_baselines.tip: Scores simple reference models, such as the city average, on the same test areas. The full model should beat them.

stage_cv_curve.label: Distance test
stage_cv_curve.tip: Tests the model again with bigger areas held out, to see whether it stays accurate farther from any reading.

stage_s4.label: Cooling by amount
stage_s4.tip: Works out how much cooling each amount of every change brings, from a small step to a large one.

stage_s5.label: Scenarios
stage_s5.tip: Works out the cooling of the scenarios set up for the project, each with a likely range.

stage_climate.label: Future climate
stage_climate.tip: Sets the cooling against the warming expected in future climates.

stage_s6.label: Cause checks
stage_s6.tip: Separate statistical checks that the cooling comes from the change itself and is not a coincidence in the data.

stage_s7.label: Budget plan
stage_s7.tip: Finds where a fixed budget buys the most cooling, then checks that plan with the full model.

stage_finish.label: Write the report
stage_finish.tip: Writes the run's record of files, its report and the method notes.

canopy.name: Trees & canopy
canopy.oneLine: More tree cover shades streets and cools the air around it.

impervious.name: Less paving
impervious.oneLine: Swapping pavement for soil and plants keeps the ground cooler.

albedo.name: Cool roofs & surfaces
albedo.oneLine: Lighter roofs and pavements reflect sunlight instead of soaking it up.

add.label: Add
add.help: Adds this much everywhere you chose.

floor.label: Bring up to at least
floor.help: Raises places below this level up to it; places already above stay as they are.

fill_headroom.label: Use available planting space
fill_headroom.help: Plants trees on this share of the open ground that can take them (not buildings or roads).

set.label: Set to exactly
set.help: Every chosen place gets exactly this value.

scale.label: Multiply by
scale.help: Multiplies today's value in every chosen place.

ceiling.label: Cap at
ceiling.help: Lowers places above this level down to it; places below stay as they are.

to_percentile.label: Bring up to a citywide level
to_percentile.help: Brings each chosen place up to the level that this share of the city already reaches.

per_cell.label: Place by place (plan, brush or file)
per_cell.help: A different change for each place, from a saved plan, brush strokes or an imported file.

take_away.label: Take away
take_away.help: Takes this much away everywhere you chose.

bring_down.label: Bring down to at most
bring_down.help: Lowers places above this level down to it; places already below stay as they are.

confident_cools.sentence: The whole likely range is below zero: the change cools.

confident_warms.sentence: The whole likely range is above zero: the change warms.

could_be_zero.sentence: The likely range includes zero: the effect could be too small to tell apart from no change.

unknown.sentence: This result has no uncertainty estimate, so there is no likely range.

saturating.label: Diminishing
saturating.tip: Each extra step cools less than the last, so the cooling levels off.

linear.label: Steady
linear.tip: Each extra step cools about the same, across the amounts tested.

sigmoid.label: Slow start, then strong
sigmoid.tip: Little cooling at first, then a sharp gain once enough is added, then it levels off.

censored.label: Hit the limit
censored.tip: Still cooling at the largest amount the space allows, so we cannot see where it would level off.

below.label: Below caution
below.tip: Heat index under 80 °F. No heat-risk category.

caution.label: Caution
caution.tip: Heat index 80–90 °F. Tiredness is possible with long exposure or activity.

extreme_caution.label: Extreme caution
extreme_caution.tip: Heat index 90–103 °F. Heat cramps and heat exhaustion are possible.

danger.label: Danger
danger.tip: Heat index 103–125 °F. Heat cramps or heat exhaustion are likely; heat stroke is possible with long exposure.

extreme_danger.label: Extreme danger
extreme_danger.tip: Heat index 125 °F or more. Heat stroke is highly likely.

good.label: Good
good.sentence: Predicts well in places it was not trained on.

fair.label: Fair
fair.sentence: Gets the broad pattern right in places it was not trained on; treat street-level detail with care.

limited.label: Limited
limited.sentence: Struggles in places it was not trained on; use the results as a rough guide only.

trustRanges.narrow: Its prediction ranges are too narrow: real values fall outside them more often than stated.
trustRanges.wide: Its prediction ranges are wider than they need to be.

quickTrust.tip: How reliable the quick estimate is for this change. The full model is always the firm answer.

line.good: The quick estimate is reliable for this change.
line.hatched: Rough in the hatched areas — run the full model for a firm answer.
line.rough: The quick estimate is rough for this change — run the full model for a firm answer.

preview.label: Rough estimate here
preview.note: The quick estimate is less reliable in the hatched places. Run the full model for a firm answer.

result.label: Less certain here
result.note: Conditions in the hatched places go beyond anything measured in the city.

states.no_checkpoint: Model not available for this run — quick estimate only
states.cold: Model loads when you run it
states.busy: Model busy — your run will wait its turn
states.incompatible: Model not available for this run — quick estimate only
states.error: Model could not load — see Advanced options

engine.noModelNoEstimate: Full model not available for this run — build the quick estimate above to explore changes
engine.noCheckpoint: Full model not available — this run did not save its trained models

ssp126.label: low emissions
ssp126.tip: Emissions cut fast this century. The world ends up about 1.8 °C (likely 1.3–2.4 °C) warmer than pre-industrial by 2081–2100 (IPCC).

ssp245.label: moderate emissions
ssp245.tip: Emissions roughly follow current policies. The world ends up about 2.7 °C (likely 2.1–3.5 °C) warmer than pre-industrial by 2081–2100 (IPCC).

ssp370.label: high emissions
ssp370.tip: Emissions keep rising through the century. The world ends up about 3.6 °C (likely 2.8–4.6 °C) warmer than pre-industrial by 2081–2100 (IPCC).

ssp585.label: very high emissions
ssp585.tip: Fossil-fuelled growth with the highest emissions. The world ends up about 4.4 °C (likely 3.3–5.7 °C) warmer than pre-industrial by 2081–2100 (IPCC).
